definition: A class of reinforcement learning algorithms that directly optimize a parameterized policy by estimating the gradient of expected reward with respect to policy parameters.
details: Policy gradient methods, including PPO, are widely used in RLHF pipelines to fine-tune language models based on reward signals derived from human preference data.

explainer.lead: Policy gradient is a class of reinforcement learning algorithms that directly optimize a parameterized policy by estimating the gradient of expected reward with respect to policy parameters. It is the foundation of methods like PPO used in RLHF.

tiers.eli5: The agent gets a nudge in the direction that makes its rewarding actions more likely next time.
tiers.practitioner: Used in RLHF pipelines to fine-tune language models from human-preference reward signals, typically via PPO. A pitfall is reward hacking, where the model exploits the reward signal rather than improving behavior.
tiers.paperLevel: The policy, parameterized by theta, is updated by ascending an estimate of the gradient of expected reward with respect to theta. The estimate is stochastic, so variance reduction and trust-region constraints are standard.

explainer.example: A language model is fine-tuned with PPO against a reward model trained on human preference comparisons.
